text.tspan: Pair a Browser and Open a Terminal
How the owner's browser goes from sidecar api open to a live terminal WebSocket on the loopback Browser listener, without a token ever appearing in a URL that is sent.
Only a process that can open the 0600 Local socket can start pairing.
The command finds the socket through
The code rides in the URL fragment, which a browser never
sends, so it stays out of request lines, proxy logs and
2. Exchange the code for a session token
The pair page reads the fragment, clears it from history, and spends the code once.
Hashed-script CSP, no framing, no-store, no-referrer.
JSON body plus X-Sidecar-Request: 1, from the listener's
Redeem code; bind token to this Origin
The page stores the token in localStorage as
sidecar.session and navigates to next on the same origin.
Browsers cannot set headers on a WebSocket, so the bearer token buys a short-lived ticket.
Bearer bound to this Origin; per-client limits
Host before upgrade; ticket and Origin after
A Host refusal is a 421 before the upgrade; every other
refusal is a 44xx close code, since a browser cannot read a
One v0 protocol stream, hello first
